ts


const waitFor = async (predicate: () => boolean, ms = 5000): Promise<void> => {
  const step = 5
  let waited = 0
  while (!predicate() && waited < ms) { await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, step)); waited += step }
  if (!predicate()) throw new Error('the engine never answered in time')
}

their own stream-json protocols and shows their work as reviewable, undoable
steps inside a local Obsidian-style vault.

The three brains — and the law about them:

Claude Code (claude) — full wire, the default engine. Signed in with
the owner's own account; the app never borrows credentials.
agy (Google's Antigravity CLI) — the second engine. Its wire is
implemented (stdin stream-json, --conversation resume, event:'result');
a signed-in live turn has never been driven yet — recorded as unproven.
Pictures are not sent through agy (the app says so in words).
Ollama — not an engine. It is the free local brain server: the
app (or the owner) runs it at 127.0.0.1:11434, and Claude Code uses its
models when a brain is explicitly named. Engines are EXACTLY two; this is
law.

Process & security shape (every wall is code, tested):

Renderer is sandboxed; the preload bridge is the only door; every IPC
answer checks the parsed origin (user-info smuggling and stray file: fail).
Navigation is locked — a link cannot walk the window away; external links
open the real browser.
The extension's server requires the pairing token (x-oddbrain-pair);
unpaired captures are dropped with the reason logged.
Downloads: official URL pinned, redirect hops allowlisted by host, size caps
(see §8.1), zip-safe unpack (declared and measured caps, path-traversal
refused).
Packaged binary: Electron fuses flipped (no ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, no
NODE_OPTIONS, no inspect).
Interface is served over loopback http (never file://) so origins are real.
5. Every feature — what it is and how it is supposed to work per his wishes
5.1 The turn (the heart)
He types an order (or watches, or a recipe, or a memory pass — all ride
the one send path).
The engine is spawned by absolute path, shell-quoted on Windows, with the
machine's registry PATH merged in; empty model choice = the engine runs as
itself (no door forced, no invented model — gemma4:cloud is banned).
Words stream in live (--include-partial-messages), thinking blocks fold.
A file-touching step raises a permission card: what it wants, the diff
or the command, Allow / Deny. Allow takes the file's old copy FIRST
(checkpoint before forward; a failed checkpoint DENIES rather than allows
blind). Deny reaches the engine as a real deny.
The turn ends with an honest summary: tokens, time, what changed — and a
Restore for every change, including files the engine created from
nothing.
Approval gears: Ask me / Plan first / Auto-edits / Full speed — Full
speed turns the cards off and says so in the gear's own label.
5.2 The engine strip & thinking (his explicit wishes)
The strip above the composer is collapsible (chevron, remembered), and
force-unfolds whenever a permission waits — Allow/Deny can never hide.
Thinking blocks are collapsed by default everywhere. Open one and every
thinking block stays open from then on (one shared flag,
thinkingOpen.ts). A live-writing block still unfolds while it runs.
The title-bar dot is green only while a turn is literally live. No
colored dots anywhere claim "installed" or "working" — words instead
(installed · 2.1.302, not installed). The "fake green dots / fake model
names" round (4fb6c15) is the reference.
5.3 Engine bay & Connectors
Engine bay (in Settings → Engine): engine cards with on-face version
proof and path-on-hover, a Re-scan that skips the remember-cache,
detection that probes absolute spots FIRST (npm dir, .local\bin, Programs,
and the app's own staging ground …/oddbrain/engines/<id>/app), the
downloads column, watch-mode setup, model/gear/vault pickers.
Connectors pane (ConnectorsSection.tsx): three cards — Claude Code,
agy, Ollama — each stating the machine's actual answer and the one action
that improves it (Use this engine / copyable install line / official page /
knock on 11434 and count the brains). Check all re-asks every door.
5.4 Models & local brains
The model menu always offers "the engine's own choice — its own login"
first, then ONLY what a machine source produced. Cloud chips (:cloud),
sizes for local ones.
Ollama: start/stop/status of the staged copy from the Engine bay;
"Model stays loaded" = OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 on the serve process (a
runtime promise, a machine flag as the switch).
5.5 Vault & memory (the second brain)
Default Documents/ASSistant/AI-Brain (or chosen folder), seeded with the
canonical second-brain structure: 00 System … 10 People, 90 Archive,
templates, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rulebooks the engine must read.
Sources land as write-once notes (conversations, browser captures, imports,
laptop files, a11y trees) — never silently edited after the fact.
Memory pass: one press sends the reflect-order through the send path;
the engine writes what mattered into the memory files itself.
Keep-or-forget review, dead/ambiguous link checks, blacklists
(never-capture paths) honored everywhere.
5.6 Artifacts
Every file the engine writes can preview in-app (HTML / Markdown / code /
SVG / charts), pop out into its own window, export to PDF, be rewritten
(the engine revises; versions kept; any version restorable). The artifact
styler can pour one of the 16 design token sets into generated HTML.

5.7 Browser extension (the capture law)
Chrome MV3 extension ships inside the install. LAW: capture everything on
screen except the blacklisted paths, default ON (the owner overruled the
judges' default-off twice). Pages/selections/a11y trees flow through the
paired loopback door into the vault as Sources. Popup: pairing, blacklist,
status.

5.8 Stores & packs
OddBrain store (shipped): folder+https indexes, sha-256 digests, tamper
refusal shown before install. Packs = skills + prompts + themes. Starter,
Looks, Prompt-starters, Anthropic skills ship in the box.
Anti-skeleton law: a pack theme carries its own FULL stylesheet
(css), applied after the app's own so it wins; a css-only theme is valid;
a test refuses any shipped theme without one. The six shipped themes have
real, visibly different styles.
Engine marketplaces (design approved, not built — his go pending):
Phase 2 = Claude Code plugin marketplaces via claude plugin marketplace add <repo> run as a carded command (the engine installs its own things —
never hand-copied files). Phase 3 = agy's catalog when Google ships one.
One store page, labeled sources, no auto-sync.
Plugins, skills, connectors are distinct features with distinct surfaces — never lumped.
5.9 Appearance & motion
16 design systems (nexu-io/open-design, Apache-2.0): Claude, Linear,
Apple, Stripe, Notion, Vercel, Airbnb, Glassmorphism, Neobrutalism,
Editorial, Retro, Dashboard, Shadcn, Minimal, Modern, Default. Settings →
Appearance → Design system applies one to EVERY screen through the
app's tokens (palette, type, radii, shadows, transcript size); the system
owns accent + reading type while active; one look at a time (a pack theme
and a design system retire each other).
Plus: theme (system/light/dark), 5 accents with WCAG-checked ink, width,
transcript size, reading font, motion modes (System/Calm/Balanced/Playful/
Still), mascot words, row explanations.
Motion kit: 76 scenes + a loader, 304 status words, 8 roles mapped to
real app states (resting / idle / thinking / working / making / waiting /
searching / done). Every animation reachable, all pausable (Still, OS
reduced-motion), never blocking. The animated brain greets on first-run and
idles by the sidebar profile.
5.10 The rest of the kit (all real, all through the one send path)
Watch mode (folder changes fire the order after quiet; deletions don't;

8. Open work, specified (so the next session can just do it)
8.1 The Ollama downloader — the measured truth and the exact fix
Measured live 2026-10-17 against https://ollama.com/download/ollama-windows-amd64.zip
(redirect chain verified: ollama.com → github.com → release-assets → 200):

Compressed 1.47 GB, 87 entries, unpacks to 1.94 GB, biggest
single file 692 MB (lib/ollama/cuda_v12/cublasLt64_12.dll).
Current code refuses it at the unpack step: unzipArchive defaults are
pack-sized (perFile 200 MB, totalUncompressed 400 MB). The download cap
(MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES) is already 2.5 GB (06da1c1).

The fix (three small pieces, all designed against the real file):

Add to src/shared/lib/engineDownloads.ts:
TypeScript

export const RUNTIME_ZIP_LIMITS = {
  files: 512,
  perFile: 1_500 * 1024 * 1024,
  totalUncompressed: 4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
} as const
In downloads.ts, the zip unpack call becomes
unzipArchive(bytes, join(root, engine, 'app'), { ...RUNTIME_ZIP_LIMITS }).
(Quality, not correctness) stream reply.body with getReader() so a
1.5 GB download shows progress ticks (~8 MB) instead of a silent hang,
enforcing the cap mid-stream; fall back to arrayBuffer for tests.
Pins to write: limits admit ≥700 MB/file and ≥2 GB total; a synthetic 250 MB
entry (impossible under the old limit) unpacks (use zlib.crc32 — Node 22+
— a pure-JS CRC over 250 MB blows the 5 s test budget); source-pin the
RUNTIME_ZIP_LIMITS call-site. Alternative he may prefer: drop the staged
download entirely — the Connectors card already recommends
winget install Ollama.Ollama, and the app finds any Ollama automatically.
His call; both are honest.

8.2 Store phases 2–3
Build per 00_LIVING_DOCS/ENGINE-STORES-DESign.md after his go: source
picker on the store page (OddBrain / Claude Code marketplace / agy), index

DECISIONS — the ledger of every "why"
MD
DECISIONS — the ledger of every "why"
Companion to HANDOVER.md. The handover is the map; this is the ledger:
every nook and cranny of the app, why it is like that, whose wish or
which lesson caused it, and what guards it so it cannot quietly regress.
Entries are grouped. When a decision came from the owner's words, his
intent is quoted or paraphrased with the date. Update this file in the
same landing that changes a decision — a stale ledger is a lie.

A. Product laws and the lessons that wrote them
#	Law	Why it exists (the lesson)	Guard
A1	No fake dots. A colored dot never claims "installed/working". Words instead (installed · 2.1.302, not installed, answering at 127.0.0.1:11434 · 3 brains).	The owner: "fake green dots." The title-bar dot showed green from a process check while every turn failed; the engine picker's green dot read "this works".	honest-defaults.test.ts (no entry.found ? 'bg-ok' in the picker; title-bar dot = turn?.state === 'running')
A2	No invented model names. Default model is EMPTY = "the engine's own choice — its own login". gemma4:cloud is banned and migrates out of saved settings.	The owner: "fake model names." The app shipped a hardcoded model the machine never had, painted everywhere as if real.	honest-defaults.test.ts (default empty; migration; no UI file hardcodes a model name)
A3	An empty model choice forces no door. A NAMED brain rides its baseUrl; no brain = no ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at all.	The owner's machine: claude-code was forced at a dead localhost door → "the brain is not answering, retry 1/2/3" forever. The Memory-pass ECONNREFUSED was this same door.	engine.test.ts, engine-process.test.ts (launch env pins)
A4	Retries must name the fix. From the third api_retry, the status says: run claude once in a terminal and sign in / check connection — still trying.	Counting retries with nothing actionable left the owner staring at "retry 3" with no next step.	engine.test.ts (wire pin), stream.ts
A5	A crashed pane says so in words. Error boundary at the app root and around every settings row: the reason + stack head + Try again.	The owner: "Connectors / store / extension pages = blank screen." React's default unmount turned crashes into silent blanks.	ErrorBoundary.tsx wraps row.body in SettingsView and <App/> in main.tsx
A6	Themes carry the ENTIRE style — "not your skeleton". Pack themes may ship a full stylesheet (css), applied after the app's so it wins; a css-only theme is valid; a design system retires the pack style and vice versa (one look at a time).	The owner, verbatim: "i said to take the entire style, you kept your skeleton." The first implementation allowed only the app's five switches and REJECTED everything else.	pack-css.test.ts, design-systems*.test.ts (shipped themes refuse to exist without a stylesheet)
A7	Everything must work on HIS machine. CI-green ≠ world-clean; the TUF A15 is the acceptance lab.	Seven real-machine breakages (spaces username ×3, PATH snapshot, blank pages, white paint, scroll) that CI never saw.	The acceptance checklist lives in HANDOVER.md §8.4
A8	Claims must survive hostile judges. Tests assert real shapes and real behavior, not flattering stubs.	The 13-round systemic failure: tests stubbed the environment instead of the platform and passed while the app broke.	Test-writing rules (§K)
B. Deliberately NOT built (and why)
Not built	Why
Buddy companion / computer-use	From the original scope triage: not taken (would promise presence the app doesn't have).
Account-gated integrations	Local-first law; accounts are the owner's own, entered at the engines themselves.
agy-via-claude-code translator	Dropped by the owner; agy's limitation is disclosed in the UI instead — accepted gap, owner's call.
The in-app Ollama downloader as the primary route	The owner: "leave the downloader things altogether." The Connectors card recommends winget install Ollama.Ollama; the app finds ANY Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 automatically. The staged copy stays secondary in the Engine bay. The measured fix (§H6) is written down for the day he wants it.
Auto-updater	No signing certificate exists; he installs CI artifacts explicitly. Silent updates would contradict "nothing machine-wide without a permission".
Marketplace auto-sync / auto-update	Approved design: "a source is added by the person; its refresh is explicit. Updates go through the same cards."
Telemetry	Local-first law. Nothing ships, nothing phones home; the interface must work with no connection.
Automatic rulebook/memory writes on a timer	The owner presses the button (memory pass, rulebook refresh). The vault's truth is his act, not a background daemon's.
Code signing	No certificate. Stated honestly everywhere: Windows will show "unknown publisher" until then.
C. Security walls — each one behind a real attack or failure
Wall	The why (attack/lesson)	Guard
Parsed-origin IPC guard (not regex)	A judge's smuggle: http://127.0.0.1:PORT@attacker.example/ passed the old start-anchored prefix regex. The door now parses components; user-info always fails; file: must be the app's own exact URL. Seven adversarial tests pin the paths an attacker would walk.	ipcGuard tests (mutant-killing: revert to prefix → userinfo case fails)
Navigation lock	A link must never walk the window (and its preload bridge) elsewhere; external links open the real browser.	lockNavigation + tests
Extension pairing	A random website must not talk to the app. Token = randomBytes(24).hex in userData/extension-pair.json, sent as x-oddbrain-pair; 401 without it — and the capture is DROPPED, never queued (page contents must not sit in browser storage without consent).	extension-pairing.test.ts, blacklist-pairing.test.ts
Outbox semantics	200 → delivered (leaves storage); 401 → drop with metadata-only record (never re-park); 403 → same; 5xx/dead network → keep for next flush; a throw keeps too; no double-parking. The old flush deleted on ANY non-throw — a judge caught the page content silently destroyed on a 500.	outbox.test.ts (six cases, real shapes)
Manifest loopback grant	The MV3 service worker had no permission for http://127.0.0.1/*, so every relay failed — the judges' first finding. The manifest grants exactly the loopback host.	extension manifest + relay tests
Classic sendResponse listener	Promise-returning onMessage is only honored from ~Chromium 148 with rollout caveats; the classic return-true + sendResponse pattern works everywhere.	background.js + messaging tests
Checkpoints before Allow	An unawaited snapshot could lose the race against the engine's write. The keep completes BEFORE the allow leaves; a failed keep DENIES instead of allowing blind; a deny never needs a keep.	claudeCode.ts answer(); engine-media.test.ts (deterministic waits, not sleeps)
Checkpoint index race	Read-modify-write runs as one queued unit per folder — 30 concurrent checkpoints left 1 record before; now 30.	checkpoints tests
Zip bomb walls	Central-directory declarations are checked up front (count, per-file, total) AND the aggregate is measured on actually-inflated bytes (a forged zero-size declaration once smuggled real bytes past the cap — a judge's 1,800-under-100 repro). Path traversal (.., drive letters, leading /) refused. Pack limits stay tight; runtime limits exist for the official Ollama zip (§H6).	downloads.ts unzipArchive + judge repro tests
Download pins	Official URL pinned, every redirect hop allowlisted by parsed host (claude.ai → downloads.claude.ai; ollama.com → github → objects/release-assets.githubusercontent.com — verified live), size caps enforced mid-stream. Byte-exact URL pins once refused the publishers' own real redirects — fixed to host-allowlists.	engineDownloads.ts + chain tests
Spawn safety	Command arrays, never shell strings — EXCEPT Windows engine spawns, which must shell (npm .cmd shims), and therefore must QUOTE paths with spaces (shellSafeCommand). The one non-fixed argument (model) is validated by MODEL_PATTERN = ^[\w.:@/-]+$ before it can reach a spawn.	command-line.test.ts, engine-detect-paths.test.ts (source-pins every spawn/probe site)
Electron fuses	Packaged binary: no ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, no NODE_OPTIONS, no --inspect.	scripts/apply-fuses.cjs, CI installer run
CSP	No remote scripts, no remote fonts, no eval; self + inline styles only; connect-src limited to self + loopback ws/http. The app must work with no connection.	src/renderer/index.html
Loopback-http interface	The renderer is served over http://127.0.0.1:<port> (never file://) so every fetch is same-origin and the API boundary sees a real Origin. Fallback file page pinned exactly so offline mode keeps a working interface.	index.ts createWindow
D. The username saga — one lesson, three bugs
His Windows name is "Nishad Islam Utso" — spaces. Everything below exists because of it:

The copied installer command broke at C:\Users\Nishad (bare join(' ') display). → displayCommandLine quotes any piece with whitespace; copy + card both use it. Guard: command-line.test.ts.
Absolute-path engine spawns would break the same way under cmd /c (his own terminal proved the shape: "Processing -File 'C:\Users\Nishad' failed"). → shellSafeCommand wraps every engine spawn and every detection probe; source-pinned. Guard: engine-detect-paths.test.ts.
First run "couldn't detect" his name — the field started empty and he typed "" and moved on. → The app:whoami door (userInfo() → USERNAME env fallback) prefills the name, spaces carried untouched. Guard: handover checklist step.
Also: engine names are resolved to absolute binaries (resolveEngineCommand) before spawning — bare names only work through a fresh PATH.

E. Engine detection — the PATH saga
The snapshot bug: the machine PATH was resolved once at boot and handed out forever; engines installed later stayed invisible. Now enginePathSync kicks a background registry re-read when the snapshot is stale (>5 min), so the next detection sees the machine as it is. Guard: enginePath tests.
The bare-name bug: detection and spawns used agy/claude by name — "'agy' is not recognized as an internal or external command" is the owner's verbatim error. Detection now probes known absolute spots and reports WHERE it found the binary (found at …, path on hover): npm dir (claude.cmd), .local\bin, Programs, and — first of all — the app's own staging ground …/oddbrain/engines/<id>/app(\<binary>.exe|.cmd|<binary>) (he staged engines there by hand and the probe ignored that folder). Spawns prefer the same resolved absolute binary. Guards: engine-detect-paths.test.ts, staged-engines.test.ts (counted through join, not literal slashes — a Linux-shaped pin once failed Windows CI).
Re-scan in the bay skips the 30 s remember-cache — installed-something-just-now needs an answer NOW, not in 30 s.
F. The honesty round — one commit as reference
4fb6c15 is the canonical "we do not lie" round: fake model dead (A2), no forced door (A3), dots → words (A1), detection proof on the card face (installed · 2.1.302, path on hover), the engine strip made collapsible with force-unfold while a permission waits (Allow/Deny can never hide behind a fold; state remembered in localStorage), thinking collapsed until the owner opens one — then always open everywhere (one shared flag thinkingOpen.ts, live-writing blocks still unfold), and the six shipped themes given real stylesheets (A6). Everything above is pinned; honest-defaults.test.ts refuses regressions by name.

H. Wire facts (proven against the real binaries)
claude-code: launched --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose --permission-mode <manual|plan|…> --permission-prompt-tool stdio (--model X ONLY when a brain is named; --resume <id> on relaunch). Proven against real v2.1.300: manual makes the CLI ask; stdio routes the question to the app.
Deny shape: the CLI rejects a bare deny — the deny must carry message (proven v2.1.300).
control_request/can_use_tool → permission card; the app answers control_response with subtype:'success' and behavior: allow|deny{message}.
api_retry → status line (A4). permission_denied by the engine itself → shown, never swallowed. Failed tool_result → news, not silence.
stderr tail (600 chars) surfaces on a non-zero, non-deliberate close: "engine closed with an error: …".
Ollama: tags at /api/tags; :cloud suffix / remote_model marks cloud brains; keep-alive env NUMBER -1 (G). Serve process owned by the app (Start/Stop in the bay); a runtime the owner started himself stays his — the app never kills what it did not spawn.
agy: stdin stream-json; resume via --conversation; the app reads event:'result' as the turn's end; pictures NOT sent (the app says so in words); its model list is plan-gated and only appears once signed in; a signed-in live turn is recorded unproven until driven on his machine. Test stand-ins carry the marker 1.0.0-ob-shim (TEST STAND-IN…) so a fake can never masquerade as the real wire.
Claude brain routing: a provider key rides the ENGINE's env (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) — the app itself never calls the provider. Machine Anthropic credentials are stripped from the inherited env on every launch (the app never borrows his account), and clearing a key stops the engine only if the engine was launched with THAT provider's key (sessionAuthProvider).
I. UI decisions — the why behind each visible thing
One send path. Chat, watch, recipes, memory pass, battles, split, quick-ask — all through the same engine send, so every guarantee (cards, checkpoints, journal) holds once and holds everywhere.
The engine strip (above the composer): a RECORD, not a transcript — resume carries context forward; honest phase names; token totals; queue ("In the line"); Stop/Copy/Edit/Hand off/Compact/Review buttons each with a real title explaining itself. Collapsible per the owner; force-unfolds on a waiting permission.
Thinking blocks: collapsed by default; opening one opens them all (shared flag); live-writing stays open while writing. His rule, exact.
Title-bar dot: green only while a turn is live (A1). The Vault chip tells the truth too: green only when keeping is actually ON — "a green Vault while nothing is written would be the one kind of lie this app forbids."
Model menu: "the engine's own choice — its own login" first (A2), then machine-produced entries with cloud chips or GB sizes.
Appearance lives in window storage, not the machine settings file — deliberately: "an accent colour is a preference about reading, not a fact about the computer," and it makes the browser preview honest too.
Accent ink is readability, not decoration: every accent carries its ink chosen for ≥4.5:1 (violet deepened for white text; amber carries near-black). accent-contrast.test.ts computes the ratios so no hue can ship unreadable.
Motion kit honesty: 76 scenes + 1 loader, 304 words, 8 roles; every scene reachable (rotation through real states); the word travels with the animation it was measured for (the kit's variant map); a word is flavour — it never replaces the honest state name beside it. One pause rule for every reason (Still, OS reduced-motion, off-screen, the six-instance budget, a one-shot that finished): ob-still stops everything; the kit's shipped scene files are never modified.
Quiet scrollbars, blinking caret, empty-state mascot ("Dozing") — reading comfort is a feature; the transcript is where he lives.
Menu bar (File/Edit/View/Go/Help): every item does a real thing — New chat, Settings, Go-to-screen; no decoration.
Single instance: a second launch focuses the window you already have.
Quick-ask window: global hotkey, minimal box, "the same engine, the same cards" — same guarantees in a small surface.
First run: steps (name prefilled from the machine — D3; engine pick with real detection; vault folder with default), animated brain greeting, finish gates into the app. The animated mascot also idles by the sidebar profile row; the sidebar carries search, new chat, nav, "No conversations yet" honesty, and the profile row into Settings.
Settings search filters rows by terms and auto-opens the first matching section, so the pane never sits blank next to results; per-section Reset restores safe defaults.
Voice: a speak button on assistant messages when the platform supports TTS — read-aloud is a small, local, honest feature.
Error boundary copy speaks to a person: what broke, that the rest still works, the reason to send along, Try again (A5).
J. Data decisions — the vault and its promises
Structure: Documents/ASSistant/AI-Brain by default (or chosen), seeded with the canonical folders (00 System … 10 People, 90 Archive), templates (Person, Knowledge Note, Source kinds…), and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rulebooks the engines must read. Fresh checkouts boot quiet (seeds are canonical texts).
Sources are write-once: conversations, browser captures, imports, laptop-file references, a11y trees — never silently edited after the fact; review is a separate, explicit act (Keep-or-Forget).
Conflict settle: when structure integrations disagree, files are kept side-by-side and the OWNER settles: Keep-mine / Use-new / Both / Combine — recorded.
Link rules: dead and ambiguous links checked, exact-path; templates exempt; the rulebook refresh runs only when the owner presses it.
Blacklist law: never-capture paths are honored by the app, the extension, and the popup alike — one door, parity-tested.
Activity & Undo: every change journaled (09 Activity & Undo); restore is byte-exact, including files the engine created from nothing.
Handoff: a finished turn becomes a vault document any later session can continue — and is copied to the clipboard in the same action.
Compaction: conversation → brief, fresh session, brief rides along — the record is kept even as the context resets.
Checkpoints: queued per folder (C); the old self is kept BEFORE the allow leaves; restore works for edits AND creations.
Warm boot & boot order: the warm-up runs AFTER the bridges exist (a judge caught warm-up racing registration — boot-order.test.ts pins the source order); warm/keep-loaded/startup flags are machine facts (appFlags.ts), the renderer reads them through guarded doors and says honestly when it's a demo.
K. Process discipline — how this repo is run
One landing = one commit, pushed HEAD:v3 HEAD:main together; CI is the truth (checks ×2 + installer ×2). A red X on ONE branch with the identical commit green on the other = flake: re-run the failed jobs before suspecting the code (done via API; the junit comment bot posts failures "in its own words" on the commit).
The sandbox's git index rots between turns (reverts to an ancient commit; remotes vanish). Recovery law: back up ONLY this round's files → git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/v3 → re-apply → verify the status list is exactly the round's files → gate → commit. NEVER git add -A on a rotted tree without that reset (one near-miss shipped 612 stale files into a commit — caught before push by the missing remote, then redone cleanly).
The gate runs from apps/03_oddbrain (a wrong cwd once fetched a bogus tsc@2.0.4). npm ci --ignore-scripts + node node_modules/electron/install.js (node_modules evaporates between turns; electron's postinstall is skipped by --ignore-scripts).
Smoke: built app opens under xvfb; SMOKE OK SCROLL OK … errors=0 warnings=0 — a WARNING is already a failure; the scroll chain is PROVEN on the built app (forces overflow, demands real movement — the chat-scroll bug from the real machine can never return silently).
Test-writing rules: assert against real shapes (the judge lessons); source-order pins for boot; deterministic waits, never fixed sleeps (the engine-media flake); platform-neutral pins (count through join); jsdom only where DOM is real; read the FULL runner output (a silent grep once matched nothing and looked green).
Patches: exact-literal replaces with loud failure on miss; read back after JSX edits; heredocs standalone with a final print.
Counts are updated every landing (README / JUDGE-BRIEF ×2 / CHANGELOG bullet) — a handover that drifts is a lie with better manners.
Workspace hygiene: ≤ ~128 MB snapshot budget, English-only outputs, the AI-slop rule (no filler, no promotional varnish — say what it does and stop).
Sandbox downloads: /tmp is ~1 GB tmpfs — big files go to /var/tmp (the Ollama zip is 1.47 GB).
CI machine deps: xvfb + libnss3/libnspr4/libasound2t64 (workflow), plus the full GTK set locally when electron's dist is re-provisioned.
L. Store & marketplace rules (design approved, build pending his go)
One page, labeled sources (OddBrain / Claude Code marketplace / agy) — no blended results that hide provenance. Browse = capped GET reads; install = the ENGINE'S OWN command (e.g. claude plugin marketplace add <repo>) shown first on a permission card — the app never assembles plugin folders by hand (that is how formats drift). Phase 2 needs: the source picker on the store page, marketplace index readers (same fetch caps as the pack store), result cards (name, author, source badge, install command), and a live probe of the real claude plugin marketplace surface on his machine before any claim. Phase 3 (agy) waits for Google to ship a catalog. Nothing runs at app boot — marketplaces are entered, never listened to.

The Cliché Visual Palette

The "AI Startup" Gradient: An absolute obsession with indigo-to-purple-to-blue gradients. You will see this looping on headline text, card borders, or as a giant, soft blurred glow in the dark-themed background. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Acid Accents on Near-Black: A generic dark mode that relies entirely on a pitch-black background paired with a single, overly bright neon/acid accent color (like electric lime or hot pink). [1]
Overused Aesthetic Fillers: Backgrounds littered with subtle dot patterns, fine geometric grid lines, or a warm cream/sand "premium parchment" color as a default fallback for light mode. [1, 2]
2. "Container Soup" (Fake Hierarchy)

Cards Inside Cards: Instead of making real decisions about typography, sizing, and whitespace to separate content, AI wraps everything in a box. You'll see cards nested inside cards, or a bordered box holding a single line of supporting text that never needed a frame. [1, 2]
Aggressive Bento Grids: Forcing completely unrelated features into a perfectly symmetrical bento box grid layout where every block has identical rounded corners. [1, 2]
Visual Flattening: Symmetrical layouts where every single widget, stat, and feature receives the exact same size, icon weight, title, and description length. When everything is emphasized equally, nothing is emphasized. [1, 2]
3. Broken Information Architecture & Layout Slop

Micro-Copy Jargon & Emojis: Headlines that say a lot but mean absolutely nothing (e.g., "Revolutionizing scalable intelligent experiences" or "Unlock your potential. Elevate your workflow."). These are frequently paired with random emojis standing in for actual designed icons.
The Predictable Hero Setup: A universal layout formula consisting of: a rounded pill badge at the top → a massive centered gradient headline → a muted gray subtitle → two standard primary/secondary buttons.
Suspiciously Uniform Copywriting: Severe over-application of the em dash (—) in UI labels, menu options, and buttons. [1, 2, 3, 4]
4. Broken UX Logic (The Functional Giveaways)

The "Everything Everywhere" Problem: AI lacks context on user journeys. It will often place a data entry table immediately next to a data entry panel, which sits right next to a data export panel—all visible at the exact same time. It completely misses the art of progressive disclosure (hiding complex details until needed).
Lazy Menu States: Selected items in navigation bars that look incredibly uneven or rely purely on a thin, disconnected stroke/border line.
Missing System States: AI designs for the perfect, static mockup. It almost always forgets to design for empty states, loading spinners, errors, or permission dialogs. If a dashboard has zero data, it simply breaks visually or stays perfectly clean instead of showing a helpful onboarding state.

OddBrain UI/UX specification
For the app agent. Implement this in apps/03_oddbrain. Reference build: OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html (open it, click through the tabs; it uses the real kit SVGs at the app's real scale).

Rule zero: keep the scale that exists today. Every number in §2 is measured from the current build. This spec does not resize the product. It completes it.

1. What changes, in one paragraph
The chat becomes an actual chatbox (user bubbles, a plain reply column with the mark, one working strip). The working strip speaks the kit: when the engine is thinking or working, the mascot shows the scene that matches the word it is saying, and every word in the 304-word vocabulary already maps to a scene. Settings gains a live miniature of the home screen, so every Appearance choice is seen before it is kept, and the Appearance page fills its width instead of floating in it. The sidebar footer loses its utilities; only the person's name and a small animated brain remain, and clicking it opens Settings. The app opens with the assembly scene at full window size and the wordmark crawling in, once per launch, with no box around it. All 77 kit scenes are reachable and visible somewhere in the product. Nothing in the visual language changes: same type sizes, same spacing, same palette, same restraint.

3. The anti-slop contract
Banned outright. Each has the rule that replaces it.

Banned	Our rule
Indigo to purple to blue gradients	Flat accent fill. The accent is one colour, chosen by the person.
Inter everywhere	System stacks only. Segoe UI on Windows is the app's voice.
Gradient text	Text is ink. Emphasis is weight, never paint.
"Introducing" badge, pills over headings	No badges. A screen says what it is in one heading.
Glowing halo, blurred aura	Nothing glows. Depth comes from one border and one background step.
Frosted glass, backdrop blur	Opaque panels.
Icon tiles, squircle icon containers	Icons sit directly in the row, 15px, no tile.
Identical feature cards in a grid	Rows with real hierarchy. No bento. No equal-weight grids.
Cards inside cards	One frame maximum per area. A card never contains a card.
Side-stripe accent cards	No stripes. Accent appears in controls and state, not decoration.
Giant "10M+" numbers, vanity stats	No invented numbers. Counts only when real and useful.
"01 / 02 / 03" step labels	No numbered decoration. Steps named by what they do.
Pulsing green dot, fake "live"	The only live signal is the mascot in the working strip.
"Supercharge", "unlock", "elevate", "revolutionize"	Plain verbs. "Open", "save", "run", "stop".
Em dash in UI copy	Period, comma, or colon. Sweep existing strings.
Beige plus italic serif "parchment"	Light theme is cream with upright sans. No italic display type.
Unnecessary green dots, fake online signs	Status is words. "Local" is a word, not a lamp.
Emoji as iconography	Line icons at 15px, or the kit artwork. Never emoji.
Copy voice. Sentence case. Verb first on buttons. One line of explanation, then stop. Empty states say what will appear, not how exciting it is. No exclamation marks.

6.4 Working strip
Sits directly above the composer, inside the thread width. Height 28. Contents left to right:

Mascot, 24px, playing the scene for the current state and word.
Honest state label at 12.5 muted: Thinking, Working, Reading, Waiting for you.
When "Mascot mood words" is On: a middot and the flavour word, 12.5 muted.
Rules:

Scene choice follows the role: thinking, working, making, waiting, searching. The word is chosen from that scene's own word list, so the word and the drawing can never disagree.
The word changes every 3.6 to 5.0 seconds. The same word never repeats twice in a row.
On completion the strip swaps the mascot for a 40px one-shot (confetti, shades-drop, or sparkle, chosen by turn hash), plays once, holds 1.4s, then the strip fades.
Still, or OS reduced motion: the scene is frozen on its first frame, the word does not rotate, the one-shot is skipped.
The strip is the only live indicator in the product. When it is absent, nothing else claims the engine is alive.
Over 300ms of any wait anywhere: the loader scene (loader-eye-roll) at 24 to 64. Never a spinner, never a skeleton.
6.5 Empty state
resting role scene at 104 with its mood word under it when mood words are On. Heading 30px: "Morning, Friend." (time of day aware). One line 13 muted: "How can I help? The engines run on this machine." Three suggestion rows: 13px, radius 12, one border, 44px high, left icon 14. No cards in a grid. No stats.

6.6 Composer behaviour
Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line. While a turn runs the send button becomes stop (32 square, border, ink). Attachments appear as one line above the textarea, 12.5, with a thin x. No pill chips.

Stick to bottom while streaming. If the reader scrolls up more than 80px, stop pinning and show "Jump to latest" as plain 12.5 muted text at the bottom right of the thread, no pill, no shadow.

9. The opening
Every launch, once, full window. No card, no box, no border, no progress bar, no percentage.

9.1 Sequence
Time	What happens
0.00	Canvas is --color-bg. Mark centre at 44% height.
0.02	assemble injected at clamp(280px, 52vmin, 520px), --duration-scale: 0.55, container overflow: visible so the parts are seen entering from beyond the mark's own edges, i.e. from all over the screen. The scene is the shipped file, unmodified.
0.90	Wordmark "OddBrain" at 30px, weight 500, letter-spacing -0.01em, ink, 26px under the mark. Letters rise 10px, rotate -1.5deg to 0, fade in, 240ms each, 24ms stagger. If mood words are off, nothing else is shown.
1.90	Sequence done. Overlay holds.
ready	The home screen paints under the overlay; overlay fades 220ms and unmounts. It never reveals a half-built screen.
9.2 Rules
Once per process launch. Not on the quick window, not on artifact pop-outs, not on window restore, not on reload inside Settings.
Any key, click, or tap after 0.25s skips to the end state and dismisses. The skip never shows a flash of the app first.
OS reduced motion or Still: static mark and wordmark, 300ms fade in, dismiss at ready, no flight, no stagger.
If the app is not ready when the sequence ends, the finished mark and wordmark simply stay. No looping, no pulsing, no spinner.
The wordmark uses the app's own face (App sans stack), not a logo font, so it matches the product's voice.
10. Interchangeability
The nine Appearance options are independent and compose. State, persist, and apply them in this order every launch: theme, accent, size, font, width, motion, mood words, explanations, quick window. Storage key stays ai-assistant.appearance with a version field.

Guarantees that must hold for all 16,200 combinations:

No layout overflow at 940 × 620.
Accent surfaces always use --accent-ink.
Transcript options never change chrome, nav, or settings type.
Width options never change the sidebar or settings panes.
Motion options never change layout, only duration and play state.
Every option survives reload and app restart.
Reset section returns the section to defaults, including the preview.
11. Accessibility floor
Focus: 2px accent outline, 2px offset, plus a 4px --color-bg shadow. Visible on every interactive element, mouse clicks excluded.
Contrast: body 13.84 (light) and 15.59 (dark). Muted on panel 4.94 after the token fix. Accent inks per §2.3. Never place muted text on --color-card in light below 12px without checking.
Landmarks: one main, nav with a label, the sidebar as aside with a label. One h1 per screen.
Every icon button has an accessible name. Every state change that matters (turn started, waiting for permission, turn finished) is announced through one polite live region, throttled to 1 update per 2s.
Hit areas: 28 minimum, 40 for primary actions.
prefers-reduced-motion and the Still option both stop all kit motion, including the launch and the preview.

13. Acceptance
A build passes when all of these are true, measured on the running app, not read from source.

Launch plays once per process; a second window does not play it; any key skips; reduced motion shows a 300ms fade; the overlay never reveals an unpainted app.
The sidebar footer has exactly one row. Clicking it opens Settings at You. Browsing maps exists there and opens the map.
All nine Appearance rows change the preview before the click returns, and persist across a reload.
Every accent, in both themes, holds its ink ratio (4.86, 5.08, 6.48, 7.67, 5.22) and every bg-accent label uses --accent-ink.
Kit coverage is 77 of 77, and every role pool resolves to at least one existing file.
In the thread, only two bordered elements exist: a permission card and a code block. Everything else is type and hairline.
The working strip shows a word that belongs to the scene on screen, changes it within 5s, never repeats it twice in a row, and freezes under Still.
No em dash exists in renderer copy (grep '—' src/renderer returns only comments and no user-facing string).
No banned pattern exists: no linear-gradient on text, no blur over 24px, no dot or grid background, no pulsing dot element, no emoji in source strings.
All 16,200 appearance combinations render at 940 × 620 without horizontal scroll.
Focus ring is present on every interactive control, including the footer row and every pill.
The empty chat shows mascot 104 with the mood word only when the option is On.
14. Out of scope
Backend, engines, vault, extension, installer. This is a UI/UX pass: components, tokens, copy, motion, and the tests above. The kit artwork itself is not redrawn; it ships byte-exact.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html from the real repo kit.

Reads: apps/03_oddbrain motion SVGs, motionKit.ts pools, motionKitData.ts motions,
resources/icon.svg. Writes one self-contained page. No network, no fonts.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import glob

BASE = "/home/user/repo-2f05/apps/03_oddbrain"
OUT = "/home/user/OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html"

def read(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return f.read()

# 1. the 77 scenes
motion_dir = os.path.join(BASE, "src/renderer/src/assets/motion")
scenes = {}
for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(motion_dir, "*.svg"))):
    scene_id = os.path.basename(path)[:-4]
    scenes[scene_id] = read(path)
assert len(scenes) == 77, f"expected 77 scenes, found {len(scenes)}"

# 2. motions (id, duration, words)
kit_data = read(os.path.join(BASE, "src/shared/lib/motionKitData.ts"))
motions = []
pattern = re.compile(
    r'\{ id: "([\w-]+)", name: "([^"]*)", category: "([^"]*)", duration: ([\d.]+), '
    r"loop: (?:true|false), energy: '(\w+)', defaultWord: \"([^\"]*)\", words: \[([^\]]*)\] \}"
)
for m in pattern.finditer(kit_data):
    motion_id, name, category, duration, energy, default_word, words_raw = m.groups()
    words = json.loads("[" + words_raw + "]")
    motions.append({
        "id": motion_id, "name": name, "category": category,
        "duration": float(duration), "energy": energy,
        "defaultWord": default_word, "words": words,
    })
assert len(motions) >= 76, f"parsed only {len(motions)} motions"

# 3. role pools
kit = read(os.path.join(BASE, "src/shared/lib/motionKit.ts"))
block = kit[kit.index("ROLE_POOLS"): kit.index("The kit", kit.index("ROLE_POOLS"))]
pools = {}
for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+): \[([^\]]*)\]", block):
    role, items = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    if role not in {"resting", "idle", "thinking", "working", "making", "waiting", "searching", "done"}:
        continue
    pools[role] = [s.strip().strip("'\"") for s in items.split(",") if s.strip()]
assert len(pools) == 8, f"expected 8 role pools, got {list(pools)}"

# every pooled id must exist as a file
for role, ids in pools.items():
    for i in ids:
        assert i in scenes, f"pool {role} references missing scene {i}"

covered = set().union(*pools.values()) | {"assemble", "loader-eye-roll"}
missing = sorted(set(scenes) - covered)
print("coverage:", len(covered & set(scenes)), "of", len(scenes), "| not in pools:", missing or "none")

# 4. the mark
mark = read(os.path.join(BASE, "resources/icon.svg"))

# 5. stamp
template = read("/home/user/ref_template.html")
def js(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/")

html = (template
        .replace("<!--MARK-->", js(mark))
        .replace("<!--SCENES-->", js(scenes))
        .replace("<!--MOTIONS-->", js(motions))
        .replace("<!--POOLS-->", js(pools)))

with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(html)

size = os.path.getsize(OUT)
print(f"wrote {OUT}  {size:,} bytes  scenes={len(scenes)} motions={len(motions)}")

OddBrain UI/UX implementation specification · revision 2
MD
OddBrain UI/UX implementation specification · revision 2
Owner-approved direction, updated 17 October 2026. Implement in apps/03_oddbrain. Open OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html first. This revision replaces the previous nine-option UI/UX spec, not merely supplements it.

The previous reference omitted most of the owner's uploaded OddBrain.html. That omission is corrected here. Retain its eight complete looks, eight actual layouts, nine palettes, four interface styles, motion controls, scene assignments, comparison, quiz, custom mixes and shortlist. Also retain the real app's existing controls. Moving a feature is not permission to remove it.

1. Authority and boundaries
This document defines behavior, retention, measurements and acceptance. The new reference HTML demonstrates the complete visual direction and interactions.
The owner's uploaded OddBrain.html remains the inventory source. This revision reorganizes it; it does not discard its options.
Current-app behavior is the real implementation. The inspected source is commit 2f05dac9a5f7a191104377ef940f81e76b9ebd74. The HTML is a design preview, with scripted responses and sample records. Never replace the real engine, filesystem, provider or extension code with its simulation code.
No repo/README cleanup, new cloud service, microphone access, background telemetry, new font dependency or backend redesign is part of this pass.
Windows PC only. Minimum content window: 940 × 620. Test comfortable sizes 1280 × 820 and 1440 × 900 too. Do not grade a mobile layout as a missing product feature.
2. Keep the existing scale
These are default numbers, not suggestions to scale the whole app up. Structural choices change arrangement; density changes spacing; the text-size setting changes only conversation text.

Element	Size
Main page / empty-chat heading	30px / 1.15 / weight 600 / tracking -0.01em
Settings page heading	15px / weight 500. Do not use a 30px settings title.
Section heading	15px / medium
Body / UI	13px / 1.5
Navigation	12.5px
Metadata / transient brain reply	12px
Micro / optional row explanation	11px
Conversation text	14.5px / 1.65 by default; Small 13, Medium 14.5, Large 16.5
Code	12.5px, installed monospace stack
Standard title / navigation bar	44px. Do not stack two bars unnecessarily.
Sidebar	260px default. Preserve the real app's resize range, 200–420px, and collapse state.
Collapsed rail	56px
Main nav row / icon	28px / 15px
Primary New chat button	40px / radius 8 / 13px medium
Small control / icon button	28px minimum
Send button	32px square
Composer / panel radius	14px default. Style choice may change the radius, not text size.
Settings nav	220px; 200px at the smaller desktop width
Settings content padding	28px; 24px at the smaller desktop width
Conversation width	Narrow 640, Medium 760, Wide 1040; always bounded by available width
Main brain	180px canvas; 150px when the window height is 700px or less
Activity / footer brain	24px
Assistant identity	18px logo mark, not a tiny animated full-body mascot
Default motion	controls 160ms; small feedback 120ms; panels 220ms; easing cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)
Default face: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif. No Inter. No bundled or remote font. The original alternative type choices are opt-in; they must not resize the interface.

3. Quiet shell, full functionality
3.1 Delete decorative status furniture
No “Local” badge, local-workspace subtitle, “live” / “offline” indicator, pulsing dot, green dot, grey dot, replacement lamp, fake connection chip, prototype badge, permanent tutorial or explanatory strip at the top. Do not replace a removed dot with a differently shaped status ornament. Do not duplicate the brand in two adjacent headers.

This does not mean hiding actual task state, errors or privacy decisions. Keep these where they matter:

Engine work immediately above the composer.
A real approval request in the conversation.
Provider / inference location in the model selector and Settings, especially before sending selected context to a cloud model.
Errors next to the failed action, with a working recovery action.
Pairing information in Agent access / Connectors.
Folder-watch state next to the watch control, not in global chrome.
3.2 Sidebar footer
Exactly one button: 24px brain + person's name, 13px medium, 48px tall. No Local text, initials disc, settings cog, dropdown chevron, second utilities row or popup menu. The whole row opens Settings → You directly.

Browsing maps and apps/connections leave the footer and become Settings destinations. The same Settings entry must remain discoverable in every layout. An icon-only rail may use the brain as the compact entry, with the person's name in its accessible label and tooltip.

Main destinations stay Chat, Artifacts, Today, Projects, Vault and Brain. Code remains accessible through Projects and search. Keep conversation search, open, rename, pin, move to project/group and delete. Preserve drag resizing, double-click width reset, collapse persistence and keyboard access. Layout switches must not reset selection or lose a draft.

3.3 Former name-menu actions: explicit retention map
Verified against both the real repo's UserMenu and the uploaded concept's Profile menu.

Previous action	New destination	Required real behavior
Settings	You, with full settings navigation	Open directly. Ctrl+, still works.
Get API keys / Model & key information	Models & API keys	Existing provider-key forms, provider links, save/remove and custom-provider controls stay. Do not substitute the model picker for key management.
Install apps and extensions / Apps & connections	Connectors	Existing app/runtime setup, extension pairing and connection actions stay.
Plugins & community	Plugins	Existing installed packs, indexes, inspect/install, remove and pack export stay.
Browsing Maps	Browsing maps	Existing map/timeline, filters, source details and navigation stay.
A smaller window	Windows & shortcuts	Existing Quick window enable control and actual open action.
Learn more	About & help	Existing repository/help route remains reachable; desktop external links use the app's existing safe external-open bridge.
Settings → You visibly lists these destinations. None disappears just because it also has a place in the navigation.

4. Complete Appearance inventory
Appearance has five compact sub-tabs: Looks · Layout · Details · Brain & motion · My mixes. One universal Settings navigation, not an app sidebar surrounding another sidebar. No utility tray floating over the workspace.

4.1 Looks: all eight complete presets
Selecting a preset explicitly applies a bundle once. Subsequent individual choices are independent. A preset must never reassert its font, palette, layout or motion after the person changes one of those settings.

Preset	Palette	Style	Layout	Type	Motion / spacing
Warm Editorial	Paper & Plum	Editorial	Classic sidebar	Serif headings, clean system body	Balanced / Roomy
Cozy Studio	Peach Fuzz	Soft studio	Top bar	Humanist	Calm / Roomy
Quiet Minimal	Quiet Graphite	Editorial	Command first	App sans	Calm / Compact
Playful Lab	Lemon Drop	Soft studio	Bento dashboard	Humanist	Playful / Roomy
Ink & Sketchbook	Paper & Plum	Ink & paper	List + detail	Bookish serif	Balanced / Roomy
Terminal / Engineer	Midnight Ink	Editorial	Console	Monospace	Calm / Compact
Retro Desktop	Blue Hour	Editorial	Floating window	Humanist	Balanced / Roomy
Glass / Futuristic	Rose After Dark	Glass studio	Rail + list	App sans	Balanced / Roomy
Each also carries the uploaded preset's eight activity-scene assignments. Preserve those assignments. A preset sets native palette accent, “As designed” theme, 1× speed, unpaused motion, and matching interface/chat typography. It does not change model, engine, API keys, permissions, approvals, cloud consent, startup flags, quick-window enablement, chat text size, conversation width, name, saved looks, mood words or explanations.

Do not show a checkmark for a preset that no longer matches its bundle. Edited combinations can be saved under My mixes. The restrained current-app dark/sans look remains the initial default; the warm/editorial preset is not imposed on everyone.

4.2 Layout: all eight, genuinely structural
Layout	Actual structure
Classic sidebar	Resizable left navigation and recents; content to the right.
Top bar	Six sections across one top bar; no persistent left sidebar. Recents via search.
Rail + list	56px icon rail, 220px item list (180px at smaller widths), content.
Command first	Search/command entry and one focused content area. Search is clickable as well as keyboard-accessible.
List + detail	Top section navigation, 260px list, selected detail beside it.
Bento dashboard	Top navigation. Today becomes a hierarchical working dashboard: primary Continue area, projects and quick actions; a smaller approvals/artifacts/watch/sources column. Not identical tiles. Other screens remain real pages.
Console	A navigation prompt, content, and a Browse fallback for mouse users. No permanent engine-status strip or instructional transcript. The preset chooses mono; selecting this layout alone must not override a separately chosen font.
Floating window	One opaque workspace window over a flat desktop surface, tabs in its title area. No fake Mac traffic lights, fake window controls, glow or frosted backdrop.
Classic sidebar also has Full / Icon rail. Width and collapse state persist. When a layout already specifies its navigation, that structure takes precedence over the Classic-only collapse option; make that scope clear on demand, not in a permanent banner.

All layouts expose the same real screens and actions. They share application state. No layout-specific copy of a conversation store, engine connection or settings object.

4.3 Details: every palette, style and reading choice
Control	Complete option list
Theme	System, Light, Dark, As designed. As designed uses the palette's original light/dark polarity.
Palette	Neutral; Paper & Plum; Midnight Ink; Sage Notes; Peach Fuzz; Blue Hour; Lemon Drop; Rose After Dark; Quiet Graphite. Also retain OddBrain default, the real app's palette. Nine uploaded palettes plus the app default, not eight.
Accent	Palette, Violet #7350ff, Blue #4f8bf5, Teal #2fb3a2, Amber #e0a44a, Rose #e0688b. Palette restores the chosen palette's own accent.
Interface style	Editorial; Soft studio; Ink & paper; Glass studio.
Interface font	App sans; Serif headings with clean system body; Humanist (Trebuchet MS fallback); Bookish serif (Georgia fallback); Monospace (Cascadia Mono, Consolas). This retains the uploaded four typography treatments plus the current app's all-sans default.
Chat font	Follow interface; App sans; Reading serif; Anthropic Serif. The last uses installed Anthropic Serif, otherwise Georgia. Never download or bundle that font.
Chat text size	Small 13; Medium 14.5; Large 16.5. Chrome stays unchanged.
Conversation width	Narrow 640; Medium 760; Wide 1040, clamped to the available pane.
Spacing	Compact; Roomy. Row padding changes, not font sizes or hit areas.
Quick window	On / Off. Same native preference as Windows & shortcuts, not a second switch with a different value.
Mascot mood words	On / Off. Controls the scene word, not operational safety labels.
Row explanations	On / Off. Default Off. Keep safety/consent information when necessary regardless of this cosmetic setting.
No hidden couplings. Colour does not force a layout. A layout does not force a font. Motion does not change geometry. Text size does not enlarge the sidebar. A manual accent survives an unrelated style change.

4.4 Brain & motion
Motion: System, Calm, Balanced, Playful, Still. Retains the original four modes plus current-app System.
Duration scale: System/Balanced 1, Calm 1.6, Playful 0.85; divide by animation-speed multiplier. Still renders a safe static pose.
Speed: 0.5× to 1.5×, step 0.05. Never change the authored SVG's source for this.
Pause / Resume mascots, independent of motion personality. Reduced motion always takes priority; Resume must not override it.
Interactions On/Off for the front-page brain.
Cheeky replies On/Off, independent of interaction animations and professional activity words.
Mischief: Quiet, Witty, Extra. Witty default. Quiet remains responsive without wisecracks; Extra allows broader physical reactions, not constant background chaos.
Eight scene-assignment controls: Idle, Thinking, Working, Waiting, Done, Searching, Making, Resting. Every one can select from all 77 assets, including the compact loader.
Keep a scene preview/replay route, searchable gallery, categories, paging, download one SVG, download the full kit and assignment from the gallery.
Keep borrow preset behavior through Mix my own. Changing behavior does not secretly change palette or layout.
4.5 My mixes and exploration tools
Retain Mix my own, Compare, Taste quiz, Shortlist/My list, verdicts and per-choice notes, structure comparison, export choices as Markdown/JSON, copy choices, export theme and reset look. These are optional Appearance tools, not a tutorial or permanent bar over the working app.

Add named saved combinations: save, use, delete, export and import validated JSON. Save the complete appearance selection and eight scene mappings, not just its palette. Using a saved look must not restore old chats or change operational permissions.

The old “Second-pass review” control is not an appearance setting. Move it to Engine, retaining its existing behavior: report only, never approve/run. Do not remove it. Auto-keep remains under House rules. Startup and warm-runtime controls go under Windows & shortcuts and continue using their real native flags.

5. The miniature in Appearance
A small desktop-shaped Home/Chat preview stays beside all five Appearance tabs. Header says Preview, not “Home, live”. Two switches: Home / Chat. It shows the actual selected structure, palette, accent, style, fonts, size, width, spacing and mascot policy. Quick-window On adds a little matching quick-window preview.

Reference dimensions: 340px wide at a normal desktop size; 280px at narrower desktop content widths. The miniature is a 1280 × 820 composition scaled to its frame, not a phone mockup. Keep it sticky while the choices scroll. Stack it above the controls only when the content column is narrower than 620px.

In the real app, share components. Render the same Home/Chat/shell components with sample data in a read-only scaled host. Do not screenshot a fixed UI or maintain a second hand-drawn interpretation. Do not initialize a second engine, vault or permission system for the preview. Update it on the same render as the selected control, before persistence finishes. No network or external fonts needed.

“Try in workspace” closes Settings onto Chat, with the selected appearance already applied and the existing conversation/draft intact.

6. The brain: cheeky companion, calm application
The personality is witty, smug, mischievous, Shinchan-like in attitude, expressed by the owner's original brain artwork. No replacement character, copied costume, baby talk, sexual jokes, insults, guilt, dependence, demands for attention or fake claims of understanding the user. The character brings the mischief; the controls stay mature.

6.1 Interactions on empty Chat
Use the original SVG scenes, not CSS stretching of the brain artwork or a new mascot.

Input	Reaction	Example one-line reply
Body poke / Enter / Space	boop, occasional eye-roll / shades-drop	“Boop. Highly technical work.”
Head/glasses poke / Up	glasses-clean / shades-drop	“The sunglasses are load-bearing.”
Shoes poke / Down	shoe-phone / shoe-skateboard	“My shoes are taking calls now.”
Quick back-and-forth tickle	belly-laugh / cheek-drums	“Not the cheeks. I have a reputation.”
Double click	cheek-drums / belly-laugh	“Two pokes. Still no snacks.”
Drag / Left	waddle / moonwalk, then return home	“I was sitting there professionally.”
Quick flick / Right	brain-kickflip / topsy, then return home	“Completely intentional. Naturally.”
Hold	peekaboo / self-hug	“Personal space. A bold concept.”
Repeated pokes	eye-roll / pocket-panic	“Yes, yes. Premium poking service.”
Escape	Return to resting scene; clear transient reply	None
Gesture transforms affect the wrapper only. Bound dragging to roughly ±64px horizontally / ±40px vertically / ±12° and spring it back. Never drag the mascot over the composer or off the window.
A reply lasts about 2.6 seconds and occupies a reserved line. No layout jump. Mood words and the interaction reply share this slot instead of stacking lines over the greeting.
Never repeat the same reaction sentence consecutively when a pool has alternatives.
No permanent “poke me” instruction, mascot caption, action toolbar, affection meter or pet-game currency. No unsolicited talking while the user is typing.
No microphone, recording, voice imitation, speech API or autoplay sound. “Talking Tom-like” here means direct responsive physical interaction, not permission to record or transmit audio.
Never put a reaction into the transcript, dispatch a model prompt, execute a tool, grant permission or change a user's draft.
On Still, Pause or Windows reduced motion, swap to a safe static pose. No wobble, flight, spring or pointer tilt. Keyboard equivalents remain usable.
Once a real conversation is open, the large toy gives the space to the transcript. Do not keep a floating pet over active work.
7. Chat and meaningful activity
7.1 Chatbox
Empty Chat is a single compact stack: interactive brain, 30px greeting, composer, three short suggestion actions. Center the stack as a unit; do not stretch a blank area between it and the composer on tall screens.
User messages: right aligned; max 78%; card surface; radius 14 14 4 14; padding 10px 14px; no border.
Assistant: left aligned, 18px logo, 12px gap, plain reply column. No assistant bubble, “Demo response” badge, nested panel or mascot-sized identity block.
Thinking disclosure and tool events: plain typography. Only permissions and code need bordered structures inside the thread. The composer itself keeps its single border.
Keep copy/edit/retry/review/handoff/compact/checkpoints/receipt actions, accessible on keyboard focus as well as hover. Preserve code-copy, artifact opening and safe source/preview/history behavior.
Composer: Attach, Dictation, engine, model, Send/Stop. Put Cook context, Recipes, Battle, Split, Map folder, Project, Turn journal and Thinking toggle under More chat tools. Nothing is removed.
Keep streaming, cancellation, approval decisions, attachments, project scope, context limits and actual provider routing. UI reorganization must not change their meaning.
7.2 Activity strip
One 28–30px strip immediately above the composer: 24px scene + actual state + optional scene word. No card and no green dot. A working label such as “Searching” comes from the real task event; its companion word comes from the same scene that is actually displayed.

Use the kit's existing role pools and vocabulary. A word is not picked from an unrelated global random list. For example, searching can use flashlight-search / lens-inspector; reading can use read; making can use forge / assemble / architect. Custom role assignments are respected without fabricating a tool event.

Rotate only at sensible scene boundaries, with no immediate repeat, roughly once per 4–5 seconds during longer activity. Freeze scene/word rotation under Still or Pause, including across unrelated rerenders. Actual state changes still update the truthful state label. Completion gets one brief 24–40px reaction, then disappears. Error information is plain text with a recovery action, not a joke or celebratory scene.

The permission request remains the actual native action with its real diff, path and Allow/Deny controls. Other-window engine work remains observable through the existing ambient state; never answer its cards in the wrong window. Do not lose the agy limitation: it can chat, but its actions do not use this app's permission cards.

8. Opening and original wordmark
Every normal app process launch opens with the whole window as the stage. No box, rounded card, progress percentage, spinner, status label, helper instruction or tagline.

Apply saved palette/type/motion tokens before the first visible paint.
Run original assemble.svg. At normal height its authored 740px canvas is displayed at min(740px, 76vmin); below 700px use min(640px, 74vmin). SVG and its wrapper allow overflow; the window clips it. Parts visibly arrive from different screen edges. Do not crop the traveling arms/shoes/glasses into a little square.
Use duration scale 0.55, independent of normal mascot speed, for a roughly 1.54-second assembly.
Under the finished brain use OddBrain-wordmark.svg, the new hand-drawn rounded lettering. It has an intentionally irregular rhythm and a pink, slightly crooked i-dot, not a substituted font or generic word typed below the logo.
Wordmark canvas: about 228 × 50px. Letters scoot/crawl into place from about 1.03s, stagger 55ms. The B sidesteps in late; the dot drops in at about 1.82s. Settle, do not loop. The result must read clearly as OddBrain.
Ready by about 2.62s in the reference, then fade the overlay for 220ms. Native readiness is the real gate: if the app is not painted yet, hold the finished mark and name. Never reveal an unpainted app just because the timer ended.
Any click or key after 250ms skips cleanly. Remove skip listeners when done.
Still / Pause / Windows reduced motion: static original mark + complete wordmark, with only a short opacity transition. No frozen off-screen assembly parts and no letter-flight.
Once per process launch, not on Settings reload, quick-window creation, artifact popout or ordinary window restore. Settings → You / Appearance can explicitly replay it. Use a process-owned launch flag, not a renderer-only flag that makes each window run it again.

The SVG wordmark is branding, not a new body font. Its paths use currentColor and a pink token so it remains readable under every palette. Keep the original app icon and all 77 motion SVGs unchanged.

9. Settings, all retained sections
Organize into these four groups; every section is reachable by mouse and search:

Your space: You · Appearance · Windows & shortcuts · Browsing maps.
The work: Engine · Models · Performance · Agent access · Connectors.
Memory & tools: Memory · Vault · House rules · Skills · Recipes · Hooks · Plugins.
This app: System · About & help.
This is 18 sections: the original 14 plus four, not replacement placeholder pages. Keep existing section row controls, search terms, reset behavior, validation and errors. Search must also find old labels such as “API keys”, “Install apps”, “Quick window”, “pairing token” and “Browsing Maps”.

Native settings that must not be lost in the move:

Model stays loaded: same stored model preference and Ollama keep-alive behavior.
Run at startup: existing loginItem app flag.
Warm runtime: existing warmRuntime app flag, default Off.
Quick window: existing oddbrain.quickShortcut preference and bridge.quick.shortcut() path, not an appearance-only boolean that only changes the miniature.
Provider keys: existing encrypted main-process storage and model/key invalidation on key rotation/clearing. Never put secrets into the appearance JSON or saved HTML.
All existing Performance profiles/custom values; do not replace them with only the three sample profiles in the HTML.
Memory files, vault folder/structure/conflict flows, agent permissions, browser-tool entries, recipe parameters, hooks and plugin permissions.
Approval mode, second-pass review, auto-keep and checkpoint semantics.
About & help is where the design preview admits its simulation limits. Do not copy those limitations into the shipping app as if its real features were simulations. The native System page must continue showing actual reported information.

10. Colour, restraint and interchangeability
10.1 Original app default
Token	Dark	Light
Background	#141417	#f4f2ec
Panel	#1a1a1f	#ebe8df
Card	#202027	#fbfaf6
Line	#2e2e36	#dcd7ca
Ink	#ececef	#262420
Muted	#9a9aa3	#67625a
Brand pink	#e8a0b4	#b04a6a
All nine uploaded palette token sets are embedded in the reference's THEMES table. Use those values for As designed. System/Light/Dark derive matching neutral surfaces when a palette needs the opposite polarity. Do not silently map all light choices back to the same cream palette.

For accent labels choose a readable --accent-ink by measured contrast. Original five accents keep their existing white/near-black pairs. Lemon Drop's native olive needs black ink to pass; white measures only 4.43:1. For each derived palette, adjust muted text toward the palette ink until it reaches at least 4.5:1 on background, panel and card. Body text also requires 4.5:1. Links can be ink rather than an unreadable pastel accent. Use a contrast-safe focus-ring token when the raw accent is too faint against the surface.

10.2 Keep all choices without importing the banned decoration
“Use every option” is not permission to reintroduce the owner's anti-slop list. Retain the labels and functional distinctions, but clean their rendering:

Glass studio / Glass Futuristic: opaque layers, not blur, frosted glass, sheen, halos or gradients.
Playful Lab: motion and interaction personality, not notebook dots, tilted badges or icon tiles.
Ink & Sketchbook: clear outlines and selected typography, not a decorative grid background.
Retro Desktop: its palette, type and window structure, not fake Mac traffic lights or gradient title bars.
Bento dashboard: real hierarchy and unequal content weight, not identical cards flattening all information.
No purple-blue gradient, gradient text, Inter-everywhere, “Introducing” badge, glowing halo, frosted glass, icon tiles, identical feature cards, cards inside cards, accent side stripes, giant fake statistics, decorative 01/02 labels, pulsing dot, fake live indicator, “supercharge” copy, em-dash-heavy explanations, or beige-plus-italic-serif premium-parchment treatment. Optional serif type is upright. Original artwork's own lens shading is not a decorative UI gradient and is not to be redrawn.

10.3 Persist without flattening or data loss
Version the appearance schema and migrate the existing ai-assistant.appearance values. Old sans remains App sans; existing serif / anthropic-serif, width, text size, accent, motion, mascot words and row explanations all survive. Do not set all users back to the reference's default.

Layout and sidebar state can remain in their existing store. Native quick/startup/runtime flags stay in their existing owner. Export a combined appearance-only snapshot when saving a look, but exclude keys, vault contents, prompts, hooks/commands, permissions and machine-specific startup flags. Validate imports against enumerated values and valid scene IDs. Clamp numeric speed/width. Do not blindly spread imported JSON into application state.

Reset appearance resets appearance only, not saved looks or work data. Reset sample data in the reference must retain the complete chosen appearance. Deleting a saved look must not alter the current running appearance.

11. Implementation map
Prefer small shared components. Do not paste the monolithic preview program into React.

Existing / new area	Required work
state/appearance.ts + migration tests	Independent palette/theme/style/type/layout/motion choices; keep old fields; named-look serialization.
Sidebar.tsx	Footer replacement; remove duplicate utilities, not their features; preserve chat actions and resizing.
App shell / navigation state	Eight layout renderers sharing one app state. Universal Settings host.
SettingsView.tsx	Reorder all existing sections; add You/Windows/Maps/About; all former profile actions; Appearance sub-tabs. Keep original section implementations.

serve_preview.py
PYTHON
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

ROOT = Path('/home/user')
ROUTES = {
    '/': ('OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'),
    '/OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html': ('OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'),
    '/OddBrain-UIUX-Handoff.zip': ('OddBrain-UIUX-Handoff.zip', 'application/zip'),
}

class Preview(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        route = ROUTES.get(urlsplit(self.path).path)
        if not route:
            self.send_error(404)
            return
        name, mime = route
        data = (ROOT / name).read_bytes()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', mime)
        self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(data)))
        self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')
        if mime == 'application/zip':
            self.send_header('Content-Disposition', f'attachment; filename="{name}"')
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    assert (ROOT / 'OddBrain-UIUX-REFERENCE.html').is_file()
    print('OddBrain interactive preview ready on port 4187', flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(('0.0.0.0', 4187), Preview).serve_forever()

quickPreference.ts
JS
import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'
import { readStored, writeStored } from '@shared/lib/storage'
import { bridge, isDemo } from '../platform/bridge'

export const QUICK_KEY = 'oddbrain.quickShortcut'
const listeners = new Set<() => void>()
export function readQuickPreference(): boolean { return readStored(QUICK_KEY, true, value => value !== false).value }
function subscribe(notify: () => void): () => void {
  listeners.add(notify)
  const changed = (event: StorageEvent): void => { if (event.key === QUICK_KEY) notify() }
  window.addEventListener('storage', changed)
  return () => { listeners.delete(notify); window.removeEventListener('storage', changed) }
}
export function useQuickPreference(): boolean { return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, readQuickPreference, () => true) }
export async function setQuickPreference(enabled: boolean): Promise<void> {
  // The main process must accept before the UI says that the hotkey changed.
  if (!isDemo) { const result = await bridge.quick.shortcut(enabled); if (!result.ok) throw new Error('The quick-window shortcut could not be changed.') }
  writeStored(QUICK_KEY, enabled)
  for (const notify of listeners) notify()
}

look.ts
